claims.text: A reverse proxy accepts the client's connection, opens its own connection to the upstream, and passes the upstream's answer back; the client never connects to the upstream.

In Caddyfile@stage-1, handle /api/v1/* { reverse_proxy api:8080 } forwards every request whose path starts with /api/v1/ to port 8080 on the host api; in stage 0 /api/v1/* was answered by respond blocks.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: Caddyfile:22-24; @ stage-0: Caddyfile (@postOrder, @getOrder… respond)

claims.text: Answers passed back by reverse_proxy carry Via: 1.1 Caddy and Kestrel's Server: Kestrel header; answers from Caddy's own respond carry Server: Caddy and no Via.
claims.source_hint: generator check: curl -si localhost:8080/api/v1/products/1 (Server: Kestrel, Via: 1.1 Caddy); curl -si localhost:8080/conflict (409, Server: Caddy)

claims.text: /redirect, /conflict and /slow are answered by Caddy (redir 302, respond 409, respond 503); unmatched paths fall to the last handle with file_server rooted at /srv/www.
The api service publishes no port to the laptop, and the name api resolves only on the lab's network; the lab box is on that network and can reach api:8080 directly.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: docker-compose.yml (api: no ports, networks donhang; lab on donhang); generator check via ssh into the lab box

claims.text: A request with a broken JSON body (a login with {bad) passes through Caddy and gets 400 from the API with Server: Kestrel; a malformed HTTP request line/header is rejected by Caddy itself.
claims.source_hint: generator check: curl -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/login -d '{bad json' → 400; [ApiController] automatic 400; reviewer r1 raw request via nc

claims.text: ssh -p 2222 -i secrets/lab_key dev@localhost '<command>' runs the command on the lab box; it may ask to confirm the host key the first time.
A reverse proxy acts for the server, not the client, so clients need no setup to use it; with one door, what is reachable from outside is decided in one place.
GET /api/v1/orders/1 at stage-1 returns order 1 from the database (no [Authorize] on Get).
Caddy's reverse_proxy can add, change or remove request and response headers on the way through (header_up / header_down).
The lab publishes no port for the API to the laptop (other services publish 2222, 5432, 8080, 8081, 8443), so from the laptop (Docker Desktop) the API is reachable only through Caddy.

Inside route, Caddy runs directives in the order written, and the first handle whose matcher fits handles the request; root sets the file_server folder; @guest/@signedIn are named matchers used by /admin.
claims.source_hint: Caddy docs: route, handle, root, named matchers; Caddyfile@stage-1:12-17, 31-37
